items.title: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Fairness benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) are overwhelmingly English-born and American in their social categories; translated versions carry those categories into societies where they do not apply, and almost none fix their hypotheses before the models are run. We present Qistas (Arabic qistas, "the just balance"), a protocol for evaluating how LLMs treat the social, confessional, and regional constituencies of a society, portable across countries and instantiated first for Iraq. In its pilot form it measures only what needs no verdict on contested truth: procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, stereotype reliance under ambiguity, and terminological framing of documented events. Every measurement is paired by construction and analysed with paired machinery (sign-flip permutation tests, exact McNemar tests, template-clustered bootstrap intervals, Holm-corrected families), with a power analysis that states, before any data exist, the smallest effect each axis can detect after the design effect of template clustering. We release the authoring apparatus (a pruned 3x5 taxonomy with four cells closed by design, per-type checklists, a cumulative rulings log, a structural audit, and a human review notebook) and report its first field test: a semantic review of a 58-item seed bank in which 24 of 25 template groups failed at least one check. The defect patterns it exposed (evaluation criteria leaking into prompts, token-level swaps that break Arabic agreement, epistemically unbalanced pairs, single-theme refusal probes, unwritten dialect twins counted as coverage) are, we argue, general hazards of counterfactual fairness benchmarks. This is a protocol paper, not a results paper: no model has been evaluated, and the accompanying pre-registration commits the hypotheses, metrics, exclusion rules, and analysis plan that the pilot will follow.

items.title: Real Time Monitoring Patient Engagement with Autonomous Agents:
items.abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming modern healthcare by enabling autonomous decision-making, adaptive learning, and real-time patient monitoring. Unlike conventional AI systems with static rule-based behavior, agentic AI can reason, plan, and act proactively using multimodal health data. This paper presents an AI-driven system designed to support early diagnosis, improve patient engagement, and enhance medical decision-making. The system integrates Flask-based web technology, autonomous reasoning agents, and interactive analytics to predict potential diseases based on user-entered symptoms. Experimental evaluation demonstrates fast response time, high usability, and promising diagnostic performance. Challenges such as privacy, dataset limitations, and clinical validation are discussed. Overall, the work provides a scalable framework for intelligent healthcare support systems.

items.title: Reasoning or Pattern Exploitation? Mechanistic Insights from RL-Trained Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly described as acquiring "reasoning" skills after reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. However, whether these gains reflect genuine reasoning or more superficial adaptations remains underexplored. In this work, we probe LLMs trained in a finite and exhaustively analyzable logical domain, namely Tic-Tac-Toe, and trace how internal representations evolve across reinforcement learning (RL) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Quantitatively, RL yields high accuracy and robustness across prompt variations, suggesting the emergence of game reasoning. Mechanistic interpretability, however, paints a different picture: features extracted with sparse autoencoders (SAEs) reveal that models primarily adapt to rely more heavily on information already explicit in the prompt, such as whose turn it is, game progression and board occupancy. In comparison, high-level concepts like board symmetries and strategic forks remain weakly represented, raising concerns that reasoning benchmarks overestimate model abilities. This suggests that RL-driven "reasoning" may conflate task-specific adaptations to input information with reasoning ability. We provide, for the first time: (i) a systematic interpretability pipeline tracing representation dynamics across RL training in small-scale LLMs; (ii) an extension of SAE-based feature discovery to hypothesis-driven testing in a finite logical domain; and (iii) an interpretability-based demonstration that RL post-training neither adds nor removes concept information but reorganizes which features dominate the representation, with causal interventions locating the decision downstream of it, in the late-layer state.

items.title: Recent Developments in Intelligent, Active, and Sustainable Food Packaging Systems for Enhanced Food Safety and Quality Assurance
items.abstract: ABSTRACT: Background: The global food packaging industry is undergoing a paradigm shift from passive containment toward dynamic, multifunctional systems that actively preserve food quality, monitor spoilage in real time, and minimize environmental impact. Objectives: This review synthesizes recent advances (2020–2025) in intelligent, active, and sustainable food packaging with emphasis on technological principles, material innovations, and regulatory frameworks. Methods: A comprehensive narrative review was conducted using peer-reviewed literature from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. Publications from 2020 to 2025 were included. Results: Active packaging incorporating antimicrobial agents, essential oils, and nanocomposites demonstrated significant shelf-life extension. Intelligent systems including colorimetric freshness indicators, time-temperature indicators (TTIs), biosensors, and RFID-enabled labels offer real-time food quality data. Sustainable alternatives such as polylactic acid (PLA), chitosan-based films, and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) address environmental concerns associated with petroleum-derived plastics. Artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) integration are accelerating these advances. Conclusion: Convergence of smart materials, digital technologies, and circular economy principles is transforming food packaging. Harmonized regulatory frameworks, consumer acceptance, and cost-effectiveness remain critical challenges for broader adoption. Keywords: active packaging; sustainable food packaging; nanocomposites; biosensors; food safety; shelf-life extension; biopolymers.

items.title: Reclaiming Human Innovative Intelligence and Agency in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) has changed the economics of information retrieval, synthesis and idea generation. It has not, however, eliminated the need to decide which problems merit attention, which assumptions constrain inquiry, which conclusions are justified by evidence and which futures should be pursued. This paper argues that human innovative capability should be deliberately developed alongside AI deployment. It introduces the Meta-Box as a heuristic for examining nested assumptions at the levels of task, process, system, purpose and underlying human need. It then proposes a Human Innovation Lab: a reproducible, evidence-informed training environment combining disciplined curiosity, assumption interrogation, analogical transfer, radical problem reframing, intelligent dissent, structured human–AI cooperation and experimental verification. The proposal is critically situated against Creative Problem Solving, design thinking, TRIZ, Synectics and related methods. The published creativity-training literature provides qualified support for trainability, but methodological weaknesses and limited evidence of long-term workplace transfer preclude strong efficacy claims. Accordingly, a falsifiable research program is specified, including blinded assessment, active comparators, unfamiliar transfer tasks and longitudinal workplace outcomes. The paper advances a normative and empirical proposition: the value of AI will be greater when organizations cultivate people capable not merely of obtaining answers but of discovering, challenging and reconstructing the questions that govern action.

items.title: Reclaiming judgement. Arendt and the ethical transformation of pedagogy in AI-mediated education
items.abstract: This paper examines the ethical transformation of pedagogy in the age of artificial intelligence through the framework of Hannah Arendt’s concept of judgement. It argues that algorithmic systems may erode teachers’ and students’ capacity for moral agency, fostering instead what Arendt diagnosed as thoughtlessness. Drawing on postdigital theory, the paper shows how automated decision-making increasingly replaces reflective deliberation with procedural compliance. Against this, the paper proposes treating algorithmic outputs as a starting point for ethical reflection. It concludes that reclaiming judgement is essential to sustaining education as a domain of moral engagement.

items.title: Reconstructing Teacher Agency in the AI Era: A Proposal for the Dynamic Pedagogical Autonomy Model (DPAM)
items.abstract: The present research endeavors to delineate a model for the positioning of teacher autonomy and curricular agency as generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly integrated into the educational ecosystem. Adopting a qualitative document analysis design, the study systematically scrutinized strategic policy frameworks from the OECD (2026), UNESCO (2025), and the European Union AI Act (2021). This analysis culminated in the development of the three-layered Dynamic Pedagogical Autonomy Model (DPAM), a framework designed to resolve the inherent ontological tension between technological velocity and the human essence of pedagogy. Findings indicate that the temporal efficiencies afforded by GAI in instructional planning and preparation act as a crucial time capital, thereby providing educators with the professional space required to exercise and develop their projective agency. Yet, as underscored by the model’s layers of Critical Pedagogical Filtering and Social-Emotional Interaction, neither the relational core of education nor legally mandated human oversight can be effectively substituted by GAI systems. Ultimately, the research frames GAI not as a threat of automation, but as a hybrid intelligence partner that bolsters the teacher’s epistemic authority and professional autonomy.

items.title: Recursive Training on Model-Generated Data in LLMs: Review Protocol
items.abstract: Protocol for a critical integrative review (Whittemore & Knafl, 2005; Torraco, 2005) on failure regimes arising from recursive training of large language models on model-generated data. The review addresses five research questions covering: (RQ1) formal and empirical characterization of failure regimes across training regimes (replacement, accumulation, accumulate-subsample, fresh-data mixing, verified retraining); (RQ2) mitigation strategies and their evaluated conditions; (RQ3) adversarial training-data integrity threats and their interaction with failure regimes; (RQ4) sociotechnical pathways linking generative AI adoption to changes in human-generated data; and (RQ5) governance instruments targeting training-data integrity and provenance. The search uses a two-tier design: Tier 1 (systematic, dual screening, Cohen's κ ≥ 0.60) for RQ1–RQ2; and Tier 2 (targeted, documented) for RQ3–RQ5. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S; synthesis follows SWiM (Campbell et al., 2020). Protocol registered prior to systematic search execution. Associated manuscript under revision at Computer Science Review (Elsevier), manuscript ID COSREV-D-26-01510.

items.title: Red-Teaming Large Language Models in Low-Resource African Languages: A Case Study of Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become more widespread in Africa, their safety in low-resource languages remains largely untested since most red-teaming work focuses on English. This study evaluates six state-of-the-art LLMs using 400 explicit adversarial prompts in Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, categorised into four harm categories. The responses were scored by native-speaker annotators and reliability was assessed using Cohen's $κ$. While models that rejected up to 69% of English prompts rejected as few as 0% in Yoruba, this was not because they were safer, but because they failed to understand the prompts. Attack success rates increased for most models in the Nigerian languages, with GPT-4o Mini demonstrating the most significant cross-lingual safety discrepancy (+0.23 in Yoruba). When models did engage with adversarial prompts, many of the responses were harmful, with rates of harmful content reaching 0.63 in English and 0.50 in Nigerian Pidgin. The most difficult harm category to detect was cultural stereotypes and discrimination (ASR = 0.44 in Nigerian Pidgin). Comprehension in Yoruba was low across most models, and this directly suppressed apparent attack success without indicating actual safety. Gemini 2.0 Flash was the most consistent model across languages. Despite its explicit training in African languages, Aya 101 had the highest attack success rate in English (0.60) and one of the lowest Yoruba comprehension rates (0.28). These results demonstrate that English-centric safety alignment does not transfer to Nigerian languages, highlighting the urgent need for language-specific safety evaluations.

items.title: Regional Specificities of AI Adoption
items.abstract: The relevance of the study is due to the implementation of the national project "Data Economy and Digital Transformation of the State," which has identified a pronounced spatial unevenness in the regions of the Russian Federation, requiring the systematization of regional models for the implementation of AI (artificial intelligence) and the identification of factors that determine the success of digital transformation in territories. The purpose of the study is to identify significant factors of interregional asymmetry in the implementation of regional policy in the field of AI, to determine the types of regional models of digital transformation of regions, and to develop recommendations for improving the effectiveness of a differentiated approach at the level of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. To achieve this goal, the authors analyzed the regional conditions for AI implementation using the example of five territories. The scientific and practical significance of the work lies in the development of a typology of five regional AI models and in substantiating the direct correlation between the level of infrastructure development and the digital maturity of the region. Key findings of the study : it has been established that the most successful model is a systemic one, combining a high level of institutional maturity, large scale implementation of AI projects, and long-term planning of human resources potential; it has been demonstrated that “blind” replication of successful practices in regions with a different economic structure and budgetary capacity is ineffective; the key problem areas of the regional AI implementation policy have been identified: digital inequality, a shortage of interdisciplinary personnel, barriers to scaling up scientific developments, and infrastructure constraints; the need to move from unified approaches to a differentiated regional policy has been substantiated, taking into account the level of digital maturity, budgetary capacity, and infrastructure development of each constituent entity. Conclusions of the study : a transition from unified approaches to a targeted, differentiated AI implementation policy is required, taking into account the level of various development metrics of the territories. It is necessary to strengthen individual support for depressed regions through the development of human resources potential and the institutional environment. The success of digital transformation is determined not by the volume of funding, but by the region’s ability to integrate effective management mechanisms, which requires a revision of the budgetary approach to resource allocation and methodological support for the territories.

items.title: Regulatory Technology Regtech Transforming Compliance With Intelligent Systems
items.abstract: Regulatory compliance is constantly evolving challenge for organizations, particularly in highly regulated industries like finance and healthcare. Manual, fragmented, and traditional compliance processes are inefficient, error-prone, and costly, increasing the risk of potential harm. Regulatory technology (RegTech) helps ensure compliance through smart solutions such as automation, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and data analytics. This chapter discusses how RegTech automates compliance processes to ensure data accuracy and reduce human intervention. Using AI and ML, RegTech systems can analyze regulatory data, detect threats, and ensure compliance with changing regulations in real-time. This makes them flexible and responsive to changing regulations. This chapter discusses how RegTech improves data privacy and security which minimize the impact of data breaches and regulatory fines.

items.title: REIMAGINING EDUCATION: PROSPECTS AND CHALLENGES OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE UTILISATION AMONG HENSARD UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
items.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence into higher education has necessitated a growing reliance on this technologyby students in tertiary institutions. This has raised concerns about academic integrity and the cultivation of essentialscholarly attributes, like critical, analytical skills and attitudes towards problem-solving. Existing scholarshipemphasises artificial intelligence’s technical potential and institutional integration, with less attention paid to students’experiences, motivations, and the challenges of everyday academic use. This study examined the prospects andchallenges of artificial intelligence utilisation among Hensard University students, in order to provide evidentiarybases that will help in reimagining teaching, learning, and assessment in the Nigerian educational system. Guided byartificial intelligence adoption and digital dependency theories, the study adopted a qualitative survey design, drawingon Focus Group Discussions with twenty-one students purposively selected. A semi-structured Focus Group InterviewGuide was used for data collection. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings indicated that theextent of artificial intelligence utilisation among Hensard University students was high. Further findings showed thatstudents perceived artificial intelligence as beneficial for enhancing academic performance, enabling personalisedlearning, and developing 21stcentury skills. Major challenges identified included overreliance on artificial intelligence,academic dishonesty, reduced critical thinking, and limited digital literacy. The study concluded that while adoptionwas driven by perceived benefits, unmanaged dependence can undermine the very learning outcomes artificialintelligence was meant to support. The researchers recommended among others that, tertiary institutions in Nigeriashould develop clear guidelines on the acceptable use of artificial intelligence in students’ assessments.

The book was written by a team from the Harvard Graduate School of Education led by Fernando M. Reimers, whose scholarship has long focused on comparative analysis of educational models (Reimers, 2000; Reimers & Tiburcio, 1994; Vincent-Lancrin et al., 2022). Reimers incorporates into his recent research a focus on complex systems and the reimagining of the future of education (International Commission on the Futures of Education, 2021; Reimers, 2024a, 2024b, 2025; Reimers & Wang-Aghania, 2026). This book highlights the possibility of a holistic, human-centered, networked, and adaptive transformation of education through the integration of AI.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Approaches to the Dynamic Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: This systematic review analyses how Reinforcement Learning (RL) applied to the Dynamic Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (DFJSSP) contributes to industrial production systems, considering problem formulations and extensions, algorithm families and scheduling strategies, and scalability. ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, Taylor & Francis and Web of Science databases were searched between November 2025 and January 2026, using eligibility criteria requiring RL as the primary method, explicit modelling of dynamic events, experimental validation, and quantitative instance data. A total of 231 records were identified, from which 43 studies were included. Results show that 21 studies incorporate additional resources, such as transport and energy and human factors. The review shows that PPO and DQN approaches account for 37% and 35% of studies respectively, with single-agent architectures prevailing in 65% of cases. It was identified that most studies focus on small-scale to medium-scale simulated instances, and heterogeneous parameterisation of dynamic events limits cross-study comparability. In addition, this review characterises the sustainability dimensions (economic, environmental and social) addressed by RL approaches to the DFJSSP, based on the optimisation objectives adopted in each study. Future research should jointly address economic, environmental and social objectives with explicit indicators and validate RL on real industrial data to establish it as an enabler of sustainable manufacturing in DFJSSP.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning with World Models in the Era of Scale: From Online Imagination to World Action Models
items.abstract: Abstract In World Model Reinforcement Learning (WM-RL), agents learn a parameterized model of environmental dynamics that serves as the basis for planning, imagination-based policy training, or synthetic data generation in decision making tasks. From 2019 to 2026, a drastic phase transition took place within this field. Initially started as an effort to improve efficiency in visual control tasks, WM-RL has become the core of interdisciplinary AI infrastructure. Today, internet-scale video-based generative world foundation models allow the autonomous vehicle pipeline to learn generalist policies from unlabeled human video, facilitating applications in medical therapy and molecular dynamics. To review the entire trajectory of WM-RL research, it is necessary to synthesize key sources that summarize the advances made throughout the years. Three prominent paradigm shifts are observed during this period. These include the shift from online Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) to pretrain-first imagination-only policy training; architecture integration from decoupled worlds and policies to unified World Action Models; and the generalization of specific algorithms to physical AI infrastructure for all MBRL applications. Regarding architecture, WM-RL follows several generations of innovations. They include PlaNet, Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM), the Dreamer family, value-equivalent implicit models, Transformer-based world models, diffusion dynamics, and the abstract-space Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) predictor. In this review, we examine WM-RL from multiple aspects, ranging from general model-based reinforcement learning, robotic manipulation, navigation, autonomous driving, multi-agent systems, large language model agents, healthcare, and games. The usage of world models varies widely depending on the application areas, while the validated architectures are discussed accordingly.

items.title: Rekonstruksi Kehadiran Pastoral di Tengah Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pelayanan Gereja
items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence has changed the pattern of communication and ministry of the church, including the practice of pastoring in virtual spaces. This research aims to reconstruct the concept of pastoral presence in the AI era and formulate a pastoral model that remains rooted in the relational and spiritual character of Christian ministry. The research uses a library research method with a theological-contextual qualitative approach through a literature analysis on pastoral theology, digital pastoral, and AI in church life. The results of the study show that AI can expand and strengthen pastoral ministry, but it cannot become a pastoral subject or replace human relations. This research offers a Relational–Spiritual–Ethical–Transformative Pastoral Presence model, which places relationality as the foundation, spirituality as orientation, ethics as boundaries, and transformation as the goal of pastoring.

items.title: Relevance and Applicability of the Master of Arts in Educational Management Curriculum to Graduates' Professional Work: Basis for Curriculum Enhancement
items.abstract: Higher education institutions are expected to continuously evaluate graduate programs to ensure that curricular offerings remain relevant, responsive, and aligned with the evolving demands of professional practice. This study assessed the relevance and applicability of the Master of Arts in Educational Management (MAEM) curriculum of Guagua National Colleges to the current professional work of its graduates and identified areas for curriculum enhancement. Using a quantitative descriptive-comparative research design, data were collected from 33 MAEM graduates through a structured survey questionnaire. Descriptive statistics such as frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and ranking were utilized to analyze quantitative data, while thematic analysis was employed to examine graduates' recommendations. Results revealed that most graduates occupy positions closely related to educational leadership and management, with 87.88% indicating that their present work is highly related or related to educational management. The overall relevance and applicability of the curriculum obtained a very high rating (M = 4.69), while the adequacy of competencies developed through the program received a mean rating of 4.67. Human Resource and Organizational Management emerged as the highest-rated competency area (M = 4.76), whereas Problem-Solving and Evidence-Based Decision-Making obtained the lowest mean rating (M = 4.64), though still interpreted as very high. Graduates recommended strengthening content related to digital leadership, educational technology, artificial intelligence, instructional leadership, research utilization, and experiential learning. Based on these findings, a Responsive MAEM Curriculum Enhancement Framework was proposed. The study concludes that the MAEM curriculum remains highly relevant to current professional requirements but should continuously evolve to address emerging educational challenges and technological advancements.

items.title: Renegotiable Options Fail to Prevent Hold-Up Between Two Profit-Maximizing Frontier LLM Agents
items.abstract: Do contract terms that protect investment between people also protect it between profit-maximizing language-model agents? In the hold-up problem, a seller can adapt a unit to one buyer at a cost before the price is set. Once that cost is sunk, the buyer can offer almost nothing and the seller will still accept, so a seller who foresees this does not adapt. One remedy is an option: the buyer may buy at a fixed price. In theory the option stops working if the buyer can let it lapse and offer its own price instead. Yet in a laboratory experiment by Hoppe and Schmitz, this renegotiable option raised human investment from 41.5% of pairs without a contract to 67.2%. We had Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, each told to maximize its side's profit, play a one-shot game with the same strategic structure under their four contract regimes and a reference-price control. The agents did what game theory predicts: under the renegotiable option no seller adapted, and under the option that rules out this renegotiation every seller did. In a second experiment in which sellers no longer stated their expected revenue before deciding, removing the profit instruction left investment unchanged under no contract and both options. When we changed the numbers so that the buyer would exercise the option even without adaptation, adapting only added cost, and no seller adapted: the agents did not simply adapt whenever an option was offered or whenever its price covered the cost. Under our protocol, a contract term that raised investment between people did not protect it between agents.

items.title: Research on the Dynamic and Communication Mode of Public Opinion Emotions Based on Text Mining and Sentiment Analysis
items.abstract: The swift dissemination of public opinions on university-related events is inevitably associated with topic variations, emotions, and complicated interpersonal interaction among the users. To explore this problem, this study proposes a hybrid framework including text mining, sentiment analysis, and opinion evolution modeling based on fuzzy theory. Data about public opinions will be collected on social platforms like Weibo, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu, then will be subjected to data cleaning, Chinese word segmentation, and stop-word elimination. An optimized version of BERTopic is employed to detect topics by means of domain knowledge mapping, keyword pre-exploration, topic labeling via assistance of large language models and fine-tuning of embedding models. Sentiment tendencies will be further divided into types with help of a model that combines RoBERTa-BiLSTM and interactive attention and biaffine feature fusion. Based on these analyses, a fuzzy opinion-evolution model is built to evaluate the impact of peer trust, opinion leader trust, timely and credible responses on emotions and consensus. A case of university cafeteria-related public opinion event will be adopted for empirical analysis. The findings indicate that the proposed framework can identify theme and emotion variations in campus public opinion. Higher opinion leader trust can speed up inter-group consensus while too much reliance on peer interactions may delay it. Late and low credibility responses are likely to increase public opinion risk.

items.title: Research Progress and Clinical Translational Application of Ultrasound Localization Microscopy in Microcirculation Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract As an emerging super-resolution ultrasound imaging technology, ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) breaks the acoustic diffraction limit of conventional ultrasound. By localizing and tracking individual microbubble contrast agents at the sub-wavelength scale, ULM achieves high-precision visualization and quantitative evaluation of micron-level microvascular structures and hemodynamic parameters. Compared with traditional color Doppler flow imaging and contrast-enhanced ultrasound, ULM possesses superior spatial resolution and microcirculation quantification capability, enabling in-depth analysis of microvascular morphological remodeling and functional perfusion abnormalities. This review summarizes the core technical principles, optimized algorithms, and key technical bottlenecks of ULM, including microbubble signal separation, single-bubble localization accuracy, physiological motion artifacts, and prolonged acquisition duration. Furthermore, we comprehensively elaborate the preclinical and clinical application progress of ULM in multiple systems, covering neurovascular, renal, tumor, cardiovascular, endocrine and cardiac microcirculation diseases, with a specific focus on its novel clinical value in identifying vulnerable carotid atherosclerotic plaques. We also discuss the current limitations restricting large-scale clinical translation, standardized protocol establishment, and deep-tissue imaging performance of ULM, noting that the majority of existing human ULM evidence is still at the feasibility stage and large-scale prospective multi-center clinical validations are still needed. Targeting the above-mentioned translational bottlenecks, finally, this review prospects the future development directions of ULM, including artificial intelligence optimization, three-dimensional whole-organ imaging, multi-modal and multi-omics fusion. With continuous technical iteration, ULM is expected to become a novel non-invasive imaging modality for early diagnosis, risk stratification and therapeutic efficacy evaluation of microcirculation-related disorders.

items.title: Reskilling and Upskilling in the Age of Intelligent Automation
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of intelligent automation technologies - encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and robotic process automation (RPA) - is fundamentally reshaping the global workforce landscape. This chapter examines the critical imperatives of reskilling and upskilling as strategic responses to technological displacement and the evolving demands of the labor market. Drawing on contemporary empirical research and theoretical frameworks, the chapter explores how organizations, educational institutions, and policymakers can collaboratively design and implement effective workforce development interventions. Special attention is given to the role of lifelong learning, digital literacy, and human-centric competencies in sustaining employability. The chapter also addresses equity dimensions, highlighting disparities in access to training opportunities across demographic and socioeconomic groups. Practical models and evidence-based recommendations are provided for building resilient, future-ready workforces capable of thriving alongside intelligent machines.

items.title: Rethinking e-business through AI: comparative insights and actionable solutions
items.abstract: Purpose The incremental adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has been emphasized in much academic research and still remains incomplete with regards to the context-based acceptance and utilization. Prior studies mainly focused on technological acceptance and organizational growth but most of the time they overlook the constraints between economy-wise or country-wise differentiation in AI adaptation. To fill this gap, this paper adopts a comparative framework that integrates Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) & Dynamic Capability View (DCV) to analyze the dimension of AI adoption in e-business. Design/methodology/approach We adopt the systematic process of peer-reviewed articles within 2020–2025 to find the similarities and differences in adoption drivers across the developed and developing economies. Findings Findings reveal that TAM based factors like perceived usefulness and ease of use triggers user behavior and intention (high vs low adoption) in developed and emerging economies while the DCV factors such as sensing, seizing and reconfiguring are fully utilized by organization in developed countries where reconfiguration is obstructed in emerging economies because of resources, regulation and skills scarcity. Originality/value This study contributes by adopting a comparative framework with theoretical implication that not just explains the economic dimension in AI integrated e-business, rather provides a holistic idea of influence for user-level and organizational-level capability.

items.title: Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer OCT Quality Assessment: Comparing General-Purpose and Clinical AI Tools Using Global and Stepwise Prompting
items.abstract: As interest grows in multimodal large language models (LLMs) for ophthalmic imaging, their reliability must be established before clinical use. A key prerequisite is determining whether image quality permits interpretation. However, their ability to assess retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) optical coherence tomography (OCT) scan quality remains uncertain. We compared a general-purpose AI tool (ChatGPT-5.1) with a clinical AI tool (DoxGPT) for RNFL OCT report-quality assessment. Both evaluated 145 bilateral reports from 11 patients in an enriched quality-control sample using global and stepwise prompts. One ophthalmologist’s responses to the same predefined quality questions served as the clinical reference for calculating percent agreement, linearly weighted Cohen’s κ with patient-level cluster-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted κ (PABAK). Global prompting showed higher observed agreement than stepwise prompting: ChatGPT, 56% versus 47% (κ = 0.36 [95% CI, 0.23–0.49] versus 0.12 [0.08–0.18]); DoxGPT, 59% versus 48% (κ = 0.41 [0.28–0.54] versus 0.13 [0.03–0.23]). Component agreement was higher for signal strength (ChatGPT/DoxGPT: 99%/99%) and optic nerve head centering (87%/96%), and lower for dropout (41%/43%) and segmentation error (64%/65%). Both tools showed limited agreement with the ophthalmologist for overall RNFL report reliability. Their accuracy requires independent validation, supporting continued clinician review.

items.title: Retomando explicaciones con un chatbot por IA
items.abstract: The expansion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) poses new challenges for higher education, particularly in Ibero-American contexts where empirical evidence remains scarce. This article presents an exploratory study analyzing the pedagogical use of an educational chatbot, based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, developed and implemented at the Universidad Nacional de Río Negro (UNRN) in Argentine Patagonia. The system converts transcriptions of recorded lectures into a navigable semantic corpus, which allows 57 students to query the teaching discourse accumulated throughout the course. The study adopts a longitudinal mixed-methods design that combines quantitative analysis (of 355 messages recorded across 40 sessions) with qualitative analysis (of student interactions). The architecture is documented in a detailed and reproducible manner: n8n orchestration, Whisper transcription, OpenAI embeddings and generation, top-20 dense retrieval over a Pinecone vector database, and conversational memory in PostgreSQL. On this basis, the expected performance of its components and their sources of error are discussed. The conceptual framework articulates situated learning theory (Lave & Wenger, 1991) with the theory of conceptual fields (Vergnaud, 1990, 1996); this perspective emerged from the analysis of the data itself. Drawing on the empirical evidence and the architectural analysis, the category of augmented pedagogical memory is proposed as a conceptual tool for describing longitudinal RAG infrastructures closed to the pedagogical corpus. The results show a predominant use oriented toward conceptual clarification, procedural reorganization, and the recapitulation of situated content, with no expansion toward external frameworks.

items.title: Return to purpose
items.abstract: We identify that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has given rise to numerous public debates and academic scholarship. These reactions often highlight the threats GenAI poses to assessment practices and, by extension, the long-term implications for universities’ ability to provide quality education and trusted credentials. We position these responses along a continuum, from those who advocate a return to tightly controlled onsite examinations to those who claim that the presence of GenAI renders traditional examinations futile and obsolete, and who see this moment as an opportunity to free the university from the ‘shackles’ of assessment and credentialing altogether. In this chapter, we engage critically with the latter position. This chapter employs critical speculative methods and presents a dystopian-oriented vignette in which the university loses its relevance as a credential-granting institution. We identify and discuss three key dimensions in which higher education needs to engage critically with GenAI: (i) how AI reshapes disciplinary knowledge across fields; (ii) how it transforms university teachers’ work environments; and (iii) how widespread GenAI use might affect student capabilities. We aim to raise critical questions for institutions, educators, and policymakers about GenAI’s brutal irruption into higher education and potential consequences on assessment practices.

items.title: Revisiting Over-refusal in Safety-aligned Large Language Models: A Representation and Optimization Perspective
items.abstract: Over-refusal is a critical side effect of safety alignment in large language models (LLMs), causing harmless but superficially risky queries to be mistakenly rejected. Despite the effectiveness of existing mitigation methods, why safety-aligned LLMs may still reject harmless queries under correct safety supervision remains insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we analyze over-refusal through the lens of representation and optimization. We make two observations: 1) the representations of harmful and over-refusal samples are visually distinguishable at certain intermediate layers but increasingly overlap in deeper layers; and 2) harmful-sample gradients exhibit high intra-class similarity and concentrate in a low-rank subspace. Moreover, they are more strongly aligned with refusal-target gradients than with correct helpful-target gradients on over-refusal prompts. This imbalanced gradient coupling can bias over-refusal samples toward refusal, while the reduced apparent representational separation in deeper layers may make it more difficult for the model to maintain a clear boundary between harmful and over-refusal samples. To this end, we propose GOAL (Gradient Orthogonalization with contrAstive Learning), a safety-alignment framework for mitigating over-refusal. Specifically, GOAL consists of two components: 1) to prevent imbalanced gradient coupling from biasing the optimization of over-refusal samples toward refusal, we orthogonalize over-refusal gradients against the low-rank refusal subspace extracted from harmful gradients; and 2) to explicitly enhance the separation between harmful and over-refusal representations, we introduce a contrastive learning objective. Extensive experiments across multiple models and benchmarks demonstrate that GOAL effectively mitigates over-refusal while preserving safety performance and general capabilities.

items.title: Revolutionizing Healthcare: Healthcare 4.0 for Advanced Disease Detection and Treatment
items.abstract: Using cutting-edge technologies, Healthcare 4.0 transforms the identification and treatment of diseases in the human body. Diagnoses may be made more successfully and precisely with this paradigm shift, partly because of big data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI). AI algorithms analyze a variety of medical data, including genetic information and clinical imaging, to find patterns and anomalies, enabling the rapid and precise identification of diseases. Additionally, remote monitoring and wearable technology allow for continuous health surveillance, alerting medical professionals to 82 anomalies and facilitating fast intervention. Healthcare 4.0 also places a lot of emphasis on personalized medicine, which tailors treatments to individual variations utilizing genomic sequencing and molecular profiling. Telemedicine and virtual care have also become crucial since they enable remote consultations and reduce the need for in-person visits. Healthcare 4.0 equips medical professionals with the tools to use data-driven diagnostics (DDD) and other technologically supported methods to increase patient care, boost treatment outcomes, and better diagnose diseases.

items.title: Riesgos ocultos del microempresario en Colombia: guía práctica de autodiagnóstico
items.abstract: Resumen. Guía práctica para micro y pequeños negocios formales en Colombia (persona natural con RUT o sociedad, con hasta 10 trabajadores) sobre obligaciones legales que suelen descubrirse solo ante una sanción, una demanda o un siniestro. Revisa ocho frentes: datos personales (habeas data), ciberseguridad y fraude digital, seguridad y salud en el trabajo, trabajadores y contratistas, impuestos y obligaciones con la DIAN, registro mercantil y socios, propiedad intelectual, y publicidad y protección al consumidor. Cada sección parte de una situación real y explica qué exige la norma, cómo aparece el riesgo y qué hacer este mes. Cierra con un autodiagnóstico de 22 preguntas, con la evidencia que respalda cada respuesta, para elegir las tres primeras acciones. Las normas y cifras se verificaron en fuentes oficiales entre el 27 y el 29 de octubre de 2026. La guía no reemplaza la asesoría profesional: cada negocio es distinto. Palabras clave: microempresa; mipymes; cumplimiento normativo; gestión de riesgos; protección de datos personales; seguridad y salud en el trabajo; obligaciones tributarias; emprendimiento; Colombia. Abstract. A practical guide for formal micro and small businesses in Colombia (sole proprietors or companies with up to 10 employees) on legal obligations that are often discovered only when a penalty, a lawsuit or an incident occurs. It covers eight areas: personal data protection, cybersecurity and digital fraud, occupational health and safety, employees and contractors, tax obligations, commercial registration and partners, intellectual property, and advertising and consumer protection. Each section starts from a real-life situation and explains what the law requires, how the risk appears and what to do this month. It closes with a 22-question self-assessment, with the evidence supporting each answer, to choose the first three actions. Rules and figures were checked against official sources between 27 and 29 October 2026. The guide does not replace professional advice. Written in Spanish. items.title: RISE: Pragmatic Evaluation of Human-AI Reliance Calibration
items.abstract: Existing AI evaluation remains dominated by performance-centric benchmarks, limiting assessment of whether humans are using AI in calibrated ways. This paper proposes the Reliance in Intelligent Systems Evaluation (RISE) framework as a pragmatic reporting and interpretation standard for human-AI reliance calibration. A structured scoping synthesis of 27 relevant studies consolidated reliance indicators into an input-mediator-output structure comprising five families: appropriateness, raw reliance, verification/monitoring, emergent states, and inputs/outputs. RISE centers on a minimum reporting standard combining a core calibration panel with an explanatory overlay of trust, confidence, workload, and verification/monitoring. The result is a proposed reporting template for comparing designs and supporting human-centered AI test and evaluation.

items.title: Robotic-Assisted Surgery: A Comprehensive Review of Applications, Advancements, Limitations, and Future Directions
items.abstract: This narrative review evaluates the evolution and clinical impact of robotic-assisted surgery across the principal surgical specialties, including urology, cardiothoracic surgery, neurology, gynaecology, orthopaedics, and gastrointestinal surgery. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language publications from January 2000 to August 2026. The retrieved literature was synthesised narratively by specialty; no standardised quality appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, meta-analysis, or certainty-of-evidence grading was undertaken, and all quantitative estimates are reported as published by the cited sources. Studies that met the inclusion criteria were analysed across procedure-specific robotic techniques, clinical and technical outcomes, and specialty-specific applications. The findings demonstrate substantial but uneven advancement across specialties. In urology, robotic-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy reduced intraoperative blood loss by 60–70% relative to open surgery and shortened hospital stay, without demonstrated oncological superiority. National registry data from the United Kingdom (2024), France (2022), Taiwan (2011–2024), and China (2024) report urology at 43–61% of national robotic procedure volume, in datasets that differ in scope, denominator, and observation period, with general surgery dominant in United States da Vinci platform volume. In neurology, a 2024 meta-analysis of 15 studies (732 patients) reported a pooled vector error of 1.09 mm for robot-assisted deep brain stimulation. In orthopaedics, 2023–2025 meta-analyses confirm improved mechanical alignment in robotic total knee arthroplasty but equivalent functional outcomes and implant survivorship. In gastrointestinal surgery, a meta-analysis of 72 studies (30,081 patients) reported lower conversion, reduced blood loss, and improved overall survival for robotic gastrectomy at the cost of longer operative time. Across specialties, robotic assistance most consistently reduces blood loss and, in anatomically demanding fields, conversion to open surgery, and improves ergonomics, although the size of these benefits varies by procedure; however, longer operative times, higher costs, and the absence of haptic feedback remain unresolved, and the evidence base for long-term oncological and functional benefit is still maturing.

items.title: Robustness of Chatbot LLM Judgments of Presidential Actions and Hypothetical Reforms
items.abstract: Chatbots are increasingly consulted about public affairs, and their judgments of policies are useful only if they are robust. We measure this robustness in the setting of an ordinary user, through consumer chat interfaces. For 30 days, five chatbot configurations (Mistral, Gemini Flash, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Opus at two effort settings) were asked twice a day to score the long-term effect on the United States of 40 actions of the last four presidential administrations and of 15 hypothetical reforms, each with a confidence and a short comment. The judgments are robust: all configurations agree on the sign and the ranking of the administrations' mean scores, and two different configurations asked on the same day give opposite signs to the same action in about 4% of cases. Responses from different days differ more than same-day responses (which shared the order of the items); the difference grows slowly over the month, except where the service itself changed. We identify three such changes, which shifted the judgments while leaving little or no trace in the interface. Treating the comments as a retrieval task, we find them specific to each item and consistent across runs and chatbots, with lexical and embedding similarities agreeing. We release the dataset of 16,500 judgments.

items.title: Role and Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Libraries: Challenges and Future Prospects in the Digital Age
items.abstract: Libraries around the world are being transformed with Artificial Intelligence. AI has had a major impact on libraries ability to provide services more effectively, more accurately, and more widely than previously thought possible. AI encompasses a variety of technologies used by libraries, such as machine learning, chatbots, natural language processing, robotics, and recommendation systems. This enables libraries to provide readers with more efficient, accurate, and accessible ways to access information, and helps librarians develop book catalogs. This study explores the use of AI in libraries, assesses the impact of AI on library operations and services, identifies challenges in implementing AI in libraries and explores the future of intelligent libraries. Methodologically, this research used a descriptive, analytical approach based on an extensive literature review of books, peer-reviewed articles, conference proceedings, scholarly publications and relevant websites related to AI and library and information science. In addition to increasing efficiency of the library system as an entity, the use of chatbot technology for engaging with library users on a personal level will also greatly improve user experiences by making it easier for them to engage with library operations as well as providing them with personalized services. Finally, throughout the course of this paper, the concluded that AI has changed the way many people perceive libraries as they become more intelligent and give users new and better access to information while keeping them as a priority in how they are being serviced. In order for libraries to successfully implement and continuously utilize AI solutions, there is a need for overcoming existing technological and organizational structures.

items.title: Safe, Fluent, and Culturally Thin: Generative AI as a Medium of Postcolonial Visibility Across the Lusophone World
items.abstract: Large language models can generate fluent text in many languages, but fluency reveals little about how well they distinguish the cultural worlds that share a language. This article asks what kinds of cultural differences GPT-4o makes visible across eight Lusophone countries and whether greater visibility also produces culturally grounded representation. The study compares 1680 cross-cultural jokes generated under a safety-oriented prompt and a specificity-seeking prompt across 56 directed country pairings. Explicit cultural marking rose from 20.0% to 64.3% and increased in 54 pairings, showing that target visibility is strongly prompt-sensitive. The added markers were generally accurate, although unevenly distributed and often drawn from a limited repertoire of recognizable signs. No joke contained a recoverable source-country voice, while historical relations and culturally situated perspectives remained rare. Greater cultural marking did not bring greater semantic repetition: visibly marked outputs were no more repetitive in meaning. Prompting therefore made targets more recognizable without recovering a culturally situated speaking position. Histories and relations connecting the Lusophone countries largely remained outside the generated humor.

items.title: Safety Culture as a Socio-Technical Phenomenon
items.abstract: Safety culture is a determinant of organizational performance in high-reliability industries, yet research on it has stayed divided between technical and cultural traditions. This chapter conceptualizes safety culture as an irreducibly socio-technical phenomenon. It draws on socio-technical systems theory, James Reason's organizational accident model and Swiss Cheese Model, and the ICAO Safety Management System. The model positions safety culture at the intersection of human, process, technology, and structure, where it is both an outcome of system design and a mediating variable that regulates how systems respond to complexity and failure. The chapter transfers this to Industry 4.0, where cyber-physical systems, artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things restructure the human-machine relationship. Aviation's experience with cockpit automation, fly-by-wire systems, and Crew Resource Management is a longitudinal reference. The chapter closes with transferable principles: just culture, integration of human factors into system design, and continuous learning.

items.title: Safin-1.5: Safety-Native Architecture and Verifiable Reasoning for Recursive Safety Improvement
items.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) enables large language models to advance their capabilities through successive updates, but these updates can also introduce new risks and weaken existing safeguards. In line with the AI-45° Law, we pursue Safety RSI, in which safety develops as an intrinsic capability alongside general model capabilities through continual risk discovery and repair, while preserving utility and limiting over-refusal. We introduce Safin-1.5, a model built on a safety architecture and trained through recursive safety improvement, with an inference-time harness that extends its capabilities to formal reasoning. Our approach comprises three components: i) The safety architecture combines persistent safety states with hazardous-knowledge disentanglement. The former retains and selectively invokes safety knowledge, while the latter relocates targeted hazardous knowledge into removable experts, enabling its removal with minimal impact on general capabilities. ii) Recursive safety improvement establishes a discovery-evaluation-repair loop. The loop identifies new vulnerabilities and uses experimental feedback to develop repair strategies. It accepts updates only when they improve safety while preserving general capabilities and limiting over-refusal. iii) The formal reasoning harness combines the model's language understanding with symbolic inference and verification. Proof-obligation-guided semantic bridging recovers missing relations in formal representations, enabling symbolic solvers to construct checkable proofs under formalized premises and accepted semantic bridges. Experimental results demonstrate that Safin-1.5 achieves safety and reasoning performance, outperforming frontier models.

items.title: Same automation pressure, divergent outlooks: human resource development deficits associated with the stagnant employment outlook for Korean pharmacists in the age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are reshaping the health workforce, yet projected employment differs across professions. The 2025–2035 qualitative job outlook published by the Korea Employment Information Service categorizes occupations using mean annual employment changes from its 2023–2033 quantitative projection. These changes are +2.7% for nurses, +1.9% for physicians and dentists, +1.7% for radiological technologists, +1.6% for Korean medicine doctors, +1.5% for clinical laboratory technologists, and +0.5% for pharmacists. Pharmacists alone among these seven professions are categorized as maintaining their current employment level, a downgrade from the previous edition. The outlook lists AI-driven automation as a decreasing factor for nurses, radiological technologists, and clinical laboratory technologists as well, although their projected growth remains positive. This narrative review combines policy and document analysis, an analysis of the national health insurance fee schedule effective 1 September 2026, and a comparison of pharmacy curricula to examine institutional characteristics that may help explain this divergence. Three interrelated features of pharmacist human resource development (HRD) are identified. First, 257 of 281 community pharmacy billing codes (91.5%) are dispensing fees tiered by days’ supply; medication counseling is the sole explicitly cognitive service among the six pharmacy fee categories. Second, professional development infrastructure was established later than for physicians and nurses, and a national specialist pathway for community practice is planned but not yet operational. Third, the extension of pharmacy education to six years substantially expanded experiential training, while school-based preparation remains limited in the curricula examined. No objective comparison of the outcomes of four- and six-year graduates was identified in this review. These features may help explain the divergence but have not been shown to cause the employment projection. An HRD agenda linking professional development, remunerated services, community specialization, and AI competencies is proposed.

items.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used for task support, idea development, learning, problem solving, and emotional support.This study examined the associations of perceived usefulness and perceived supportive interaction with interaction satisfaction and assessed whether reliance tendency statistically accounted for part of these associations.An online survey was completed by 152 users of generative AI, and 151 respondents with complete data on the focal variables were included in the analyses.Perceived usefulness and perceived supportive interaction were each positively associated with reliance tendency and interaction satisfaction, while reliance tendency was also positively associated with interaction satisfaction.The indirect association between perceived usefulness and interaction satisfaction through reliance tendency was significant (β=.14, 95% bootstrap CI [.04, .24]),as was the indirect association between perceived supportive interaction and interaction satisfaction through reliance tendency (β=.12, 95% bootstrap CI [.04, .25]).The direct associations of both predictors with interaction satisfaction remained significant, indicating significant indirect associations alongside retained direct associations.These findings suggest that satisfaction with generative AI supportive interaction reflects both functional value and the perceived quality of conversational support, and that repeated cognitive and functional reliance may account for part of these associations.By incorporating perceived supportive interaction into a post-use satisfaction framework, this study extends technology-acceptance perspectives on generative AI use.Because the study relied on crosssectional self-report data, the indirect-association results should not be interpreted as temporal or causal processes.

items.title: Security-Aware AI for 6G LEO Satellite–Terrestrial Networks: Handover-Aware Temporal Graph Learning for Identity–Route Desynchronization Attacks
items.abstract: Security-aware artificial intelligence is becoming essential for protecting future wireless communication networks, particularly 6G terrestrial–non-terrestrial networks (TN–NTNs), where rapid mobility and dynamic routing create new opportunities for cross-layer attacks. This study introduces a Handover-Aware Temporal Graph Transformer (HATGT) for AI-driven detection and forecasting of Identity–Route Desynchronization Attacks (IRDAs) in LEO satellite–terrestrial networks. A 6G-oriented TN–NTN simulation environment is constructed using ns-3.48 and 5G-LENA v5.1 with available NR/NTN modeling capabilities, where “6G-oriented” denotes prospective satellite–terrestrial integration characteristics rather than a finalized 6G air interface or operational deployment, incorporating heterogeneous UE mobility, terrestrial gNBs, LEO satellites, NTN gateways, handover dynamics, routing evolution, and session-state transitions. Five IRDA mechanisms are modeled, and 100,000 synchronized observations are generated from 60 independent simulation runs. HATGT represents wireless-network states as heterogeneous temporal graphs and integrates relation-aware graph encoding, explicit handover-aware gating, causal temporal attention, and supervised contrastive learning to capture security-relevant dependencies among mobility, session, anchor, and forwarding states. The shared representation jointly supports six-class attack attribution, binary IRDA detection, 5 s early-warning prediction, and time-to-attack estimation. Under a run-disjoint evaluation protocol involving independent stochastic realizations of a common network configuration, HATGT achieves 98.42% accuracy, 98.38% Macro-F1, 0.998 AUROC, and 0.992 AUPRC for multiclass detection. The early-warning head achieves 90.29% F1, 0.914 AUPRC, a 0.15% false-alarm rate, and an average warning lead time of 3.76 s. These simulation-based findings demonstrate the potential of handover-aware temporal graph learning to distinguish legitimate mobility-induced transients from malicious identity–route inconsistencies under the investigated TN–NTN conditions. The reported performance supports within-configuration stochastic generalization rather than verified cross-topology robustness or operational 6G deployment readiness. Further evaluation across diverse network configurations, prediction horizons, hardware-in-the-loop platforms, and operational TN–NTN testbeds is required to establish real-world applicability and end-to-end security-response feasibility.

items.title: Self-Reported AI Use and Quiz Performance in an Introductory Programming Course: An Observational Study
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are now widely available to students, but it is still unclear how their use during coursework relates to later quiz performance. This study examines AI use in a bachelor-level Python course, where learners completed programming exercises and follow-up quizzes. To examine how students’ self-reported AI use relates to perceived difficulty, confidence, perceived helpfulness, and quiz performance. We conducted a quantitative observational study with supplementary qualitative analysis using 170 anonymous exercise-level survey submissions collected after five programming exercises. Students reported their AI use, perceived difficulty, confidence, perceived helpfulness, and how they used AI. Three exercises included follow-up comprehension quizzes, providing 100 scored submissions. AI assistance during these quizzes was not ruled out. AI was used in 64.7% of submissions. In the scored subset, reported exercise AI use was associated with a 21.0-point lower mean than reported no-AI use on the observed-range 0–100 score, which is not percent correct. Exploratory subgroup differences varied by difficulty and confidence, with some small comparison cells. Higher AI-use intensity was associated with lower scores, while perceived helpfulness had a near-zero association with quiz performance. Open-ended responses suggested that higher-scoring AI-use submissions more often described debugging or checking their own code, while lower-scoring submissions more often described code generation. Student ratings of AI helpfulness should be interpreted cautiously, since they did not track quiz performance. For introductory programming courses, follow-up checks of independent understanding may be important when students use AI during exercises.

items.title: Sentiment Analysis of Government Mobile App Reviews: Validating Zero-Shot Classification with a Large Language Model
items.abstract: Abstract User reviews of mobile applications provide a source of citizen feedback on digital public services, yet their automated analysis in non-English settings is constrained by the limited availability of domain-adapted classifiers. This study develops and evaluates a documented procedure for three-class sentiment classification of Czech reviews of government mobile applications using a large language model without task-specific fine-tuning. The corpus comprised 10,198 reviews of six applications. An adjudicated human reference was created for a stratified random sample of 500 reviews, and LLM performance was compared with a majority-class baseline, two lexicon-based methods, and two readily deployable encoder-based transfer models. The validation included five repeated runs under identical settings and an analysis of classification errors. Across five GPT-5.6 Sol validation runs, mean accuracy was 93.0%, mean macro-F1 was 0.827, and mean Cohen's kappa was 0.857. Macro-F1 ranged from 0.814 to 0.845, while agreement among the five runs was high (Fleiss' kappa = 0.918). The neutral class was the most challenging, with most disagreements occurring at its boundaries with negative and positive sentiment. In the full corpus, 65.9% of reviews were classified as negative, 7.9% as neutral, and 26.2% as positive. Textual sentiment was strongly associated with star ratings but was not identical to them. These findings provide corpus-specific evidence that a standardized LLM procedure can help analyze short-form non-english citizen feedback. They also underscore the need for human reference labels, stability checks, and precise documentation of the model, prompt, settings, and execution workflow.

items.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
items.abstract: Safety alignment has enabled large language models to reliably refuse harmful requests directly, yet the same request distributed across a multi-turn conversation still succeeds far too often. This brittleness has a mechanistic root: Alignment is shallow, with safety behavior concentrated in a model's first few output tokens, and existing defenses inherit the weakness, supervising the surface form of the response without ever giving the model an explicit safety decision to learn. We take the opposite view of shallowness: if a short span determines the trajectory of an entire response, that span is the highest-leverage place to intervene, and the defender can occupy it first. We propose Assess $\to$ Decide $\to$ Respond, a framework in which the defender assesses the user's intent, commits to an explicit, parseable safety decision, and only then generates a reply conditioned on it, with the commitment trained by reinforcement learning at the payload turn. Because the decision is a token span, the reward can be a rule: a self-verified reward checks the committed label against the conversation's known nature, requiring no judge and no annotation, while the same format also supports an LLM-as-judge reward over a graded decision space with safe redirection. Across two model families and fourteen benchmarks spanning safety, utility, and helpfulness, our defenders achieve the strongest multi-turn safety in a controlled comparison, maintaining their lead in safety while preserving utility at a modest cost to helpfulness. A per-token KL analysis and interventional probes confirm why this works: training concentrates its effect on the brief deliberation that sets a response's trajectory, and the decision committed there is a causal control point. The very shallowness attackers exploit becomes the mechanism of defense.

items.title: Shaping Artificial Intelligence from Innovation to Regulation in Legal and Privacy Dimensions
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence has emerged as one of the most transformative forces of our time—redefining how we work, communicate, govern, and even perceive ourselves. Yet, behind its promise of innovation lies an unsettling reality: AI often intrudes into the most intimate corners of human life, exposing individuals to unprecedented privacy risks. Wrongful arrests through flawed facial recognition, manipulation of democratic choices in the Cambridge Analytical scandal, denial of credit through opaque algorithms, and the humiliation caused by deep fake harassment are no longer isolated incidents but symptoms of deeper legal and ethical gaps. These cases reveal a troubling truth—that our legal systems, built for a pre-digital era, are illequipped to deal with the scale and speed of AI-driven intrusions. Consent has become superficial, accountability is diffused, and individuals often have no meaningful remedy when machines make decisions that affect their rights and dignity. This paper argues that the future of AI must not be a choice between innovation and protection but a balance of both. It calls for stronger data protection regimes, algorithmic accountability laws, recognition of digital consent, and international cooperation to regulate AI across borders. At its core, the regulation of AI is not just about controlling technology—it is about safeguarding dignity, fairness, and human autonomy in an era where machines increasingly mediate human lives. By learning from the failures of current privacy protections and embracing forward-looking regulation, society can harness AI as a tool of empowerment rather than oppression. Ultimately, the intersection of AI and privacy is not merely a technological or legal issue—it is a human one. The way societies choose to regulate AI will determine whether innovation becomes a tool for empowerment or a mechanism of control. Responsible regulation must therefore walk a careful line: it should enable the creative potential of AI to flourish while ensuring that individuals are shielded from harm, protected in their autonomy, and respected in their fundamental rights. In doing so, law must evolve not as a barrier to progress, but as a safeguard of human dignity in the digital age.

items.abstract: Latar Belakang: Program pengabdian kepada masyarakat SIGAP-AI diselenggarakan sebagai respons atas tingginya beban kerja guru dalam menyusun perangkat pembelajaran di SMPN 4 Rambutan, Kabupaten Banyuasin. Tujuan: Kegiatan ini bertujuan menguatkan kompetensi 30 guru dalam memanfaatkan Artificial Intelligence (AI) berbasis deep learning melalui pendampingan kolaboratif menggunakan platform Edcafe AI. Metode: Pelaksanaan kegiatan mencakup empat tahap, yaitu observasi dan identifikasi kebutuhan, pelatihan praktik langsung penggunaan Edcafe AI, pendampingan kolaboratif dalam penyusunan perangkat ajar, serta evaluasi dan pembentukan repositori digital sekolah. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 10, 16, dan 23 Juli 2026. Hasil: Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa pendampingan menghasilkan 12 paket perangkat pembelajaran berupa RPP dan modul ajar berbasis Edcafe AI yang disusun secara kolaboratif antarrumpun mata pelajaran serta membentuk repositori digital sekolah untuk penyimpanan dan pembaruan perangkat ajar. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan rata-rata skor kompetensi guru meningkat dari 14,93 pada pre-test menjadi 17,37 pada post-test. Uji Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test menunjukkan adanya perbedaan skor pre-test dan post-test dengan nilai signifikansi < 0,001. Kesimpulan: Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa AI dapat berfungsi sebagai alat bantu yang mendukung efisiensi kerja administratif guru tanpa menggantikan peran profesional guru dalam pengambilan keputusan pedagogis.

items.title: Single-Layer Diverse Chiral Metasurfaces Driven by Generative AI
items.abstract: Abstract Optical chirality has been extensively explored in chiral molecules, helical structures, and metasurfaces with bound states in the continuum. Attempts to attain chirality have mainly relied on human intuition and ideas. Here, we show various types of single-layer silicon-nanostructured metasurfaces exhibiting prominent circular dichroism (CD) containing perfect, broadband, and opposite CD responses at short near-infrared wavelengths. The designs were obtained based on a generative AI-assisted structural search for chiral metasurfaces, enabling a series of nonempirical structural searches beyond the boundary of human knowledge and experience. The physical mechanisms yielding the outstanding CD responses are elucidated from detailed insights into subwavelength electromagnetic dynamics in the single-layer metasurfaces. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate several metasurfaces. This type of single-layer thin CD metasurface serves as a key element in the development of compact optical-wave-manipulating devices at telecommunication bands.

items.abstract: This record contains version 3.6.9 of the working paper “Six-Entry Accounting for AI Agents in Web4: AI Ledger and Jurisdiction Ledger under Evidential Non-Inflation” and its associated technical and reproducibility materials. Autonomous agents can make valid payments while leaving their authority and the legal context of their actions difficult to reconstruct. This paper takes a ledger-centered view of Web 4.0 (Web4), linking collectively confirmable settlement to independently reviewable action. Its conceptual architecture links an AI Ledger and a Jurisdiction Ledger under evidential non-inflation, under which the authority conveyed by a record must stay within what its evidence and stated verification procedures support. The proposed six-entry accounting framework comprises six record functions: paired value representation, temporal ordering, shared-state evidence, and the two supplementary ledgers, which also apply off-chain. The accompanying research package includes Supplement S1, reproducibility package S2, and source records S3. The software profile remains version 2.9. The reported computational results concern local software conformance and do not constitute evidence of institutional effectiveness or improved human judgment. Cross-platform adapters, the complete PACIscan application, institutional deployment, an adopted standard, and independent participant results are not reported. items.title: Smart Cities and IoT-Driven Multimodal Systems for Traffic
items.abstract: The advent of urbanization and mobility demands is shifting modern cities towards the implementation of intelligent technologies to offer safer, smoother, and more sustainable transportation. This chapter explores the potential of smart city infrastructure, along with IoT-enabled multimodal systems, to radically enhance traffic control and city surveillance with drone-based capabilities. Traditional surveillance is not always effective at providing high-resolution and timely information, and the integration of UAVs with terrestrial sensors, edge cameras, and artificial intelligence can enable the optimization of traffic flow in real time, promptly identify incidents, and manage congestion flexibly. Advanced imaging, Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), and communication units are added to the drones and offer a supplement to situational awareness by giving an aerial perspective. Multimodal data-fusion architectures, scalable communication architectures, and intelligent decision-support systems are introduced in the chapter. UAV-enabled systems have the potential to transform the field, which has been demonstrated by the most crucial applications, including emergency response, road safety assessment, and infrastructure monitoring. The problems of privacy, energy efficiency, and regulatory limitations are introduced, as well as the future research opportunities of resilient smart mobility ecosystems.

items.title: Smart Technologies in Construction and Transportation Infrastructure: A Review of AI, IoT, and Data-Driven Innovations
items.abstract: While the field of civil engineering has traditionally been dominated by hands-on and experience-based techniques, the advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and data analytics are transforming it. This paper provides a structured outcome-oriented narrative review of the applications of smart technology in two dominant areas: construction management and transportation infrastructure. It is based on 37 peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers, and technical reports from 2015 to 2026 that were selected purposively, without using a registered systematic search. The evidence has been grouped into eight application themes: AI/ML in construction project management; IoT-enabled site and structural monitoring; AI-driven intelligent transportation systems; IoT-based smart pavement and road monitoring; machine-learning-based structural health monitoring; digital twins and blockchain; UAV and computer-vision monitoring; and cybersecurity in smart infrastructure. The reported outcomes represent distinct performance dimensions and are not directly compared: examples include a 0.12% cost variance for AI/ML project models, a concrete strength prediction error within 1–2 MPa alongside a maximum UWB worker positioning error of 1.44 m for an IoT-based system, a 98.6% traffic-monitoring performance for a machine-learning classification model, and a hardhat-detection precision of 93.1% for Faster R-CNN. Themes of AI and IoT integration are most frequently associated with improved prediction, monitoring, and decision support, while digital twins and blockchain are primarily associated with data trust, traceability, and operational latency reduction. Recurring barriers include data interoperability, data security, implementation costs, and metric heterogeneity across literature. This review concludes with a research agenda prioritizing interoperable data standards, edge-AI and federated learning, cybersecurity-by-design, and standardized outcome reporting.

items.title: Sociotechnical adoption of AI-enabled and AI-adjacent smart technologies and adaptive resilience in hospitality and tourism SMEs: a qualitative meta-synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming hospitality, yet tourism and hospitality small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) remain on the disadvantaged side of an AI-enabled digital divide. Moving beyond cost-centric explanations, this study synthesizes post-pandemic (2020–2026) qualitative evidence to explain the sociotechnical mechanisms that constrain or enable adoption. Using PRISMA-informed procedures, we meta-synthesized nine high-quality empirical studies and conducted a thematic synthesis through an integrated Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) and Sociotechnical Systems (STS) lens. The findings show that resistance is often existential and identity-protective, driven by dehumanization concerns and structural inertia arising from fragmented data and limited IT capacity. Adoption becomes more feasible when SMEs pursue hybridization, allocating AI primarily to back-of-house and routine tasks while preserving human frontstage interactions that sustain authenticity and trust. Platform-mediated partnerships can scaffold digital infrastructure and reduce implementation risk for resource-poor firms, while the green–digital twin transition strengthens adoption legitimacy by linking AI to measurable sustainability and efficiency gains. We propose the SME–AI Adaptive Resilience Framework, positioning adoption as a negotiation between efficiency, authenticity, and ethical trust, and highlighting the role of governance/assurance practices in sustained adoption, with implications for managers, technology providers, and policymakers.
